sections.instruction: Complete the sentences. Use ENOUGH with one of these words. (Examples: Is there enough sugar in your coffee? — Is it loud enough for you?)

questions.prompt: He can leave school if he wants – he’s [gap].
Did you have [gap] to answer all the questions in the exam?
This house isn’t [gap] for a large family.
Tina is very thin. She doesn’t [gap].
You don’t eat [gap]. You should eat more – it’s good for you.
It’s late but I don’t want to go to bed now. I’m not [gap].
Lisa isn’t a very good tennis player because she doesn’t [gap].

sections.instruction: Complete the sentences. Use ENOUGH with the words in brackets. (Example: We haven’t got enough money to buy a car. (money / buy))

questions.prompt: This knife isn’t [gap] tomatoes. (sharp / cut)
The water wasn’t [gap] a bath. (warm / have)
Have we got [gap] sandwiches? (bread / make)
We played well but not [gap] the game. (well / win)
I don’t have [gap] the newspaper. (time / read)

sections.instruction: Put in TOO or ENOUGH. (Example: You’re always at home. You don’t go out enough.)

questions.prompt: I can’t wait for them. I haven’t got [gap] time.
You’re always tired. I think you work [gap] hard.
A: Did you have [gap] to eat? B: Yes, thank you.
You don’t eat [gap] vegetables. You should eat more.
I don’t like the weather here. It’s [gap] cold.
The radio isn’t loud [gap]. Can you turn it up, please?
She speaks [gap] fast for me to understand.
Don’t buy that coat. It’s nice but it isn’t long [gap].
He can’t reach the shelf. He isn’t tall [gap].

sections.instruction: Complete the sentences. Use TOO or ENOUGH with the words in brackets. (Examples: I couldn’t work. I was too tired. — Can you turn the radio up, please? It isn’t loud enough.)

questions.prompt: I don’t want to walk home. It’s [gap]. (far)
Don’t buy anything in that shop. It [gap]. (expensive)
You can’t put all your things in this bag. It [gap]. (big)
acceptedAnswers: isn't big enough|'s not big enough

questions.prompt: I couldn’t do the exercise. It [gap]. (difficult)
Your work needs to be better. It [gap]. (good)
acceptedAnswers: isn't good enough|'s not good enough

questions.prompt: I can’t talk to you now. I [gap]. (busy)
I thought the film was boring. It [gap]. (long)

sections.instruction: Complete the sentences. Use TOO (+ adjective) + TO (do something). (Example: (I’m not going out / cold) → It’s too cold to go out.)

questions.prompt: (I’m not going to bed / early) → It’s
acceptedAnswers: It's too early to go to bed.

questions.prompt: (they’re not getting married / young) → They’re
acceptedAnswers: They're too young to get married.

questions.prompt: (nobody goes out at night / dangerous) → It’s
acceptedAnswers: It's too dangerous to go out at night.
It's too dangerous for anybody to go out at night.
It's too dangerous for anyone to go out at night.

questions.prompt: (don’t phone Ann now / late) → It’s
acceptedAnswers: It's too late to phone Ann.
It's too late to phone Ann now.

questions.prompt: (I didn’t say anything / surprised) → I was
acceptedAnswers: I was too surprised to say anything.
